landing.metaTitle: Dr. Thaiane Lessa, full case · Lucas Portela
landing.metaDescription: How Dr. Thaiane Lessa's website was made, for a dental surgeon in Maceió, Brazil: the request, the dental council's rules, the decisions and the versions left behind.
landing.title: Dr. Thaiane Lessa
landing.lead: A website for a dental surgeon in Maceió, Brazil, built on my own, from design to code. Live since October 2026.
landing.request: Dr. Thaiane wanted a website to bring in more patients. There was no fixed deadline, but the priority was to get it live quickly.
landing.audience: Patients first: people looking for cosmetic treatment, like veneers or whitening, and people who need a problem fixed and want someone careful. The website speaks to both without mixing them up. Dentists come later, because she also works in dental marketing.
landing.rules: Advertising by dentists follows the Brazilian dental council's rules, and I learned them by researching and reading the regulations. They forbid prices, promotions, promised results and images of procedures. Before-and-after photos are allowed only with the patients' consent and with her name and license number on the image. That is why the footer carries her name, profession and license number.
landing.phoneFirst: Most patients arrive on a phone. The website started out designed for computers, and at the end of October it became phone-first. The computer layout adapts from there.
landing.sections: The top shows the place and her name. About says who she is. Services shows what she treats. Contact explains how to get there and book. Each section answers the question the one before may have left.
landing.motion: A hand-drawn monogram opens the website and flies to the header. On phones, the video stays pinned while “seu sorriso, no seu tempo” (“your smile, at your own pace”) crosses the three panels. She chose this version out of four prototypes.
landing.whatsapp: It's where patients already talk to the practice, and it's the easiest way to book.
landing.method: The same way as this website, with AI-Driven Development. I wrote the documentation: the audience, the Council's rules, every section and every motion decision. AI agents wrote the code from it, and I reviewed every version on a phone before it went live.
landing.path: There were many versions. The first ones, from May, looked like any AI-made website: a generic headline, rounded buttons and badges. Before the live version, the project went through three repositories and more than 400 commits.
landing.may1PhoneAlt: First version, from May 2026, on a phone: the headline “Seu sorriso pode evoluir com naturalidade, critério e cuidado” (“Your smile can evolve with naturalness, judgment and care”) and a menu in a rounded card.
landing.may1ComputerAlt: First version, from May 2026, on a computer: a large headline on the left and a placeholder for a photo on the right.
landing.may2PhoneAlt: Second version, from May 2026, on a phone: a bold headline about a more harmonious smile and the button “Agendar pelo WhatsApp” (“Book on WhatsApp”).
landing.may2ComputerAlt: Second version, from May 2026, on a computer: a large headline on the left and a photo of Dr. Thaiane on the right.
landing.octoberPhoneAlt: October 2026 version on a phone: the headline “sorrir é sempre uma boa ideia” (“smiling is always a good idea”), with colorful WhatsApp and Instagram icons.
landing.octoberComputerAlt: October 2026 version on a computer: the headline on the left and a video of the practice on the right.
landing.livePhoneAlt: Live version on a phone: the headline “sorrir é sempre uma boa ideia” (“smiling is always a good idea”), with dark green icons.
landing.liveComputerAlt: Live version on a computer: the headline on the left and a video of the practice on the right.
landing.result: Live since the end of October 2026. In Lighthouse, in production, it scored 88 for performance on phones, 100 on computers and 100 for accessibility.
landing.next: A section of the website for dentists, about her work in dental marketing.
landing.learned: I started from a reference, the <link>Aventura Dental Arts</link> website, which won an Awwwards prize. What I learned most was to be original instead of copying what others made.

draftcs.metaDescription: How DraftCS was made, a Counter-Strike web game built by two people: the idea, the real data, the rating review and the result card.
draftcs.title: DraftCS
draftcs.lead: A Counter-Strike web game, made with Vinicius. From the first commit to live in six days, in June 2026.
draftcs.request: Nobody asked for it. 82-0, a basketball game, had gone viral, and during the World Cup 7a0, a football one, went viral too. It was Major season, the biggest Counter-Strike tournament, so we made ours.
draftcs.audience: People who like CS and want to pass the time. A round is short: draw a roster, pick five players, simulate the run for the title and share the result.
draftcs.rules: Most APIs with player data were paid. Through research, we found open data on Kaggle and Liquipedia, and the website credits its sources. Players appear only by name and numbers: no photos and no team or tournament logos, because of image and trademark rights.
draftcs.data: 20 Majors and more than 550 players, each with the rating they had at that tournament. The team you build comes from rosters that existed.
draftcs.curation: Some players came out of the data with a rating too low or too high for anyone who follows the scene. We reviewed those cases, so the result makes sense to people who know CS.
draftcs.speed: This kind of game goes viral in days and fades in weeks. The first commit was on June 13, and the game went live at draftcs.com on June 19, still during Major season.
draftcs.card: At the end of the simulation, the game makes an image with the team, the score and the verdict, in feed, square and story formats, ready to post on X or send on WhatsApp.
draftcs.method: With AI-Driven Development. Vinicius and I wrote the documentation together, on a Discord call with a shared screen: the Major format, the game rules, the data sources and every decision. AI agents wrote the code from it, and we reviewed and tested every part. That is why almost every commit came from his account.
draftcs.path: Few versions were left behind: the look was right almost from the start and got polished along the way. The game was born as 13-0, the score of a perfect map, and three days later it became draftcs. Then came the real data, the ranking, sign-in and three languages: English, Portuguese and Russian.
draftcs.thirteenPhoneAlt: First version, from June 13, 2026, on a phone: the 13-0 brand and the headline “Monte o time dos sonhos do CS. Vai fazer 13 a 0?” (“Build your CS dream team. Can you go 13-0?”).
draftcs.thirteenComputerAlt: First version, from June 13, 2026, on a computer: the headline on the left and, on the right, a preview of a final won 13-0 with five players.
draftcs.rebrandPhoneAlt: June 16, 2026 version on a phone, already with the draftcs brand: the headline “Monte o time invencível.” (“Build the invincible team.”) and the “Jogar agora” (“Play now”) button.
draftcs.rebrandComputerAlt: June 16, 2026 version on a computer: the headline “Monte o time invencível.” (“Build the invincible team.”), the verdict card with five players and the 2.2% rarity.
draftcs.livePhoneAlt: Live version on a phone: the headline “Monte o time invencível.” (“Build the invincible team.”), with ranking, language and Google sign-in at the top.
draftcs.liveComputerAlt: Live version on a computer: the headline on the left, the verdict card on the right and the count of 20 Majors below.
draftcs.result: Live at draftcs.com since June 19, 2026. We have no numbers to show, but the game had a good spike in visits with no paid promotion.
draftcs.learned: I learned how to behave when working in a team and to be more responsible for what I agree to. And I understood why the documentation comes before the code: with the rules written down, the two of us and the agents build the same thing.

crewz.metaDescription: How Crewz was made, a social network built by two people to find others who want to do the same activity as you: the idea, privacy, the match and the design system.
crewz.title: Crewz
crewz.lead: A social network to find people who want to do the same thing as you, made with Vinicius. The first complete version took twelve days, in September 2026.
crewz.request: Nobody asked for it. Vinicius lived in Dubai, liked jiu-jitsu and riding motorcycles, and couldn't find people to do it with. He searched on Facebook, Instagram and elsewhere. We talked about it, and the idea came from there.
crewz.audience: Anyone who wants to find people with the same interests: a sport, a book, a game. In the same city or online.
crewz.rules: To open sign-in to any Google account, Google requires a public privacy policy at the app's address. That brought the terms of use and account deletion into the same delivery.
crewz.activity: Nobody joins to “make friends”. People join to do something with someone, and friendship comes later.
crewz.doors: Groups, people and events. None requires the others: you can look for just one partner, without joining any group.
crewz.anyActivity: Online or in person, with no starting niche: from jiu-jitsu to a League of Legends duo.
crewz.match: In the People deck, one side is “Not now” and the other is “Call”, like Tinder, but not for dating. Whoever was called only finds out when there's a match, and “Not now” is not saved.
crewz.levels: Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced don't fit everything. Online games have Casual, Ranked and Competitive; languages, Basic, Intermediate and Fluent; and some activities have no level.
crewz.username: Every profile has a username, to sign in without typing an email and to find people.
crewz.privacy: A public privacy policy and terms of use, and “Delete account” inside the app, right away, with no email needed.
crewz.method: With AI-Driven Development, in both our parts. Before the code, I made the design system: palette, typography, components and brand. Then we decided together, each of us wrote the documentation for our part, and AI agents wrote the code from it. My part was the design system and the visual redesign, onboarding, the profile, the home screen, the People deck, messages, search, settings, levels and usernames.
crewz.path: Few versions were left behind, because the design system came before the code. What changed was the finish: on September 24, the palette moved to petrol and cream, and the tab bar started to float. On September 28, the new brand arrived.
crewz.september21PhoneAlt: Groups tab on September 21, 2026: light cream background, a “Criar grupo” (“Create group”) button, filters and the card of a jiu-jitsu group, with the classic tab bar at the bottom.
crewz.september25PhoneAlt: Groups tab on September 25, 2026: petrol and cream palette, the crewz logo at the top and a floating tab bar.
crewz.livePhoneAlt: Groups tab in the live version: the new brand, with the orange symbol, and the “Explorar” and “Meus grupos” (“Explore” and “My groups”) tabs as pills.
crewz.result: Live at crewz-ashy.vercel.app. No users yet, because we haven't invested in promotion.
crewz.next: Decide the final name, the domain, how the app will pay for itself and how to promote it.
crewz.learned: I learned to work even more as a pair: one of us only moved forward when the other was working along. We talked a lot before anything, and every decision was made together, after debate.

About.title: About
About.text: I study Computer Science and I care about the small details: how a website feels on a phone, the timing of each animation, the words on each button.
About.methodStep1: I write the documentation: the product, the audience, the rules and every decision.
About.methodStep2: AI agents write the code from it.
About.methodStep3: I review it, test it on phone and desktop, and adjust until it's right.
About.repo: This website was built this way: the code and the decisions are in the <link>public repository</link>.
